newsitem.title: UK: EMI official says no legal basis for EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: EMI official says no legal basis for EMU delay.

text.p: European Monetary Institute (EMI) deputy general counsel Erwin Nierop said on Monday there was no legal basis for, nor any indication of, a delay to the schedule for introduction of a single European currency.
"The legal answer is very clear. There is no possibility of postponement," Nierop told a conference on European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in London.
"The final day is January 1, 1999," he said. "We're not talking about a delay because there are no indications that there will be a delay. We are completely geared towards January 1, 1999."
Nierop said the idea that EMU could go ahead on time but as an "empty shell" was unlikely to happen. "I have my doubts whether that would work," he said.
This theory is based on the idea that EMU could start on paper on schedule but without any actual members.
The EMI is the forerunner to the European Central Bank (ECB) and is charged with preparing the way for the introduction ot the euro single currency.
Nierop was asked at the conference about the importance of note issuance by the ECB.
"It will be a very important instrument. It's currently under discussion, but there are certain technical problems like who will issue, the ECB or the NCBs (national central banks)," he said.
